title: dedicated: refine autoscaling burst controls and fleet utilization reporting
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Improve Dedicated autoscaling burst controls to reduce noisy downscales and add fleet-level utilization reporting in Console. Backwards compatible and gated behind feature flag for staged rollout.
description:
Motivation: Customers using Dedicated reported oscillations when short bursts of traffic triggered aggressive downscales shortly after a burst. At the same time, platform teams lack a concise fleet-level utilization metric to reason about headroom and to tune reserved capacity. This PR implements a two-part change: (1) a burst budget allocator + smoothing logic that prevents immediate reclaiming of capacity after short bursts, and (2) a fleet_utilization metric + exporter and Console UI tile to surface utilization trends for Dedicated fleets.

Summary of changes: - Introduce burst budget allocator that tracks per-fleet burst credits and decays credits over a configurable window. This prevents immediate downscales for traffic spikes under the budget. - Add smoothing to reclaim logic: when utilization drops below target, we wait for a configurable grace period (default 90s) unless sustained low utilization is observed. - Surface fleet_utilization in metrics endpoint (percent_utilized = used_capacity / provisioned_capacity) and add an aggregator that reports 1m/5m/1h rollups. - Console: add Fleet Utilization tile and timeseries with burn-down overlays for burst budget. - Add end-to-end tests exercising burst scenarios and unit tests for allocator. - Feature-flag the new behavior under feature_flag: dedicated_burst_v2 so we can rollout gradually.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-2741) linked - [x] Unit tests added for allocator and smoothing - [x] E2E load tests in perf-canary - [x] Console UI implemented behind feature flag - [x] Docs updated (docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md) - [x] Feature flag gating and migration notes included

Rollout and compatibility: The change is opt-in via feature flag and defaults to OFF for existing fleets. When enabled, operators will see smoother downscales and a new utilization tile. No API schema changes. We will pilot on three internal Dedicated fleets for 2 weeks, then flip on for GA customers incrementally.

Notes: tuned parameters in this PR were derived from perf-canary runs and live traces from a customer incident (SUP-342). Detailed perf numbers in the Linear ticket (ENG-2810).
